$comment: Weather data colour scales, 0.1.0 draft. Generated results: results.md (python3 standards/weather-colour-scales/scales.py write). Bands are [min, max): min inclusive, max exclusive; null max is open-ended. Colours are sRGB hex.
rules: The band label or its value range is always printed beside the colour. Colour alone never carries the meaning.
Where a published scale exists it is adopted unchanged: breakpoints, labels and colours.
Brand colours (the Mzizi minerals) are never used for data scales.
Values are converted to the scale's UCUM unit at the edge before a band is chosen.
Where a swatch has less than 3:1 contrast with the surface it sits on (see results.md), it is drawn with a 1px border in the legend text colour.

scales.name: Air quality (US AQI)

source.title: Technical Assistance Document for the Reporting of Daily Air Quality – the Air Quality Index (AQI)

scales.notes: `assist` is the EPA's own ColorVision Assist palette from the same document, adopted for colour-blind display. The AQI is the US index; a national index (for example the AQHI or the EU EAQI) replaces it where a country publishes one.

scales.name: UV index (Global Solar UV Index)

source.title: Global Solar UV Index: A Practical Guide
source.claim: measured for categories and Pantone codes; the hex values are inferred from the Pantone codes and must be checked against Pantone's published sRGB

scales.notes: The UVI is reported as a whole number; round before choosing a band.

scales.name: Air temperature

source.title: ColorBrewer RdYlBu, 11 classes (ramp only; breakpoints are ours)
source.claim: inferred: the ramp values are ColorBrewer's published RdYlBu-11; the licence (Apache-2.0-style) must be confirmed at source

scales.notes: No published standard sets temperature map breakpoints. These are chosen for the African range: fine steps where people live and work, open ends at both extremes. Cold to hot is blue to red.

scales.name: Wind speed (Beaufort)

source.title: Beaufort scale breakpoints (WMO); ramp ColorBrewer YlGnBu, 7 classes
source.claim: inferred: breakpoints are the standard km/h equivalents of Beaufort forces, grouped in pairs; verify against WMO-No. 306

scales.notes: Breakpoints are Beaufort's; the colour ramp is ours, because no published wind colour standard was found.

scales.name: Rainfall rate

source.title: WMO rainfall intensity classes; ramp ColorBrewer Blues
source.edition: WMO-No. 8 (Guide to Instruments and Methods of Observation)
source.claim: inferred: the class limits (light below 2.5, moderate 2.5–10, heavy 10–50, violent above 50 mm/h) must be checked against WMO-No. 8

scales.notes: Below 0.1 mm/h nothing is drawn. Radar reflectivity (dBZ) is a separate scale, not yet adopted: the NWS progression has no published specification or licence statement found.

scales.name: Cloud cover

source.title: Okta cover classes as used in METAR (FEW, SCT, BKN, OVC); ramp ColorBrewer Greys
source.steward: WMO / ICAO (classes); Cynthia Brewer, Penn State (ramp)
source.claim: inferred: verify the okta grouping against WMO-No. 306

scales.notes: Percent cover converts to oktas by eighths before a band is chosen.
